entry.summary: #内幕消息 龙是真实存在的，但不是神话中的那种，而是类似于一种深海类生物，它没有龙鳞，全身是气孔，气膜，只能在阴雨天呈螺旋式飞行，具体原因不明，为什么要一点点让大众接受神话中的事物也是原因不明，可能除了龙还有一些震惊三观的事情需要一点点放出来，防止人类三观崩塌吧，龙正好起到了先头作用。 龙的模样并不是这种金灿灿的，而是那种水生动物般的黑灰色，还有深青色，都是以深色为主，皮肤上并非鳞片，而是气孔，皮膜覆盖的气孔，看着很像鳞片，但不是鳞片，龙会飞就是因为有这些气孔，气孔很稚嫩不能暴晒，并不是龙能呼风唤雨，而是龙只能在阴雨天出现，不然气孔会晒伤，龙并不能直上直下的飞，必须转着圈飞，直飞气孔无法进气，会导致失去平衡，龙幼年和成年变化很大，不便细说。龙并非神话故事那般神通广大，就是正常生物，也需要进食排泄，吃什么就不说了，我们现在在网络上，书上，壁画上，建筑上等看到的龙和真实的龙差别很大，身体腥臭。

RT Michael Green I want to be absolutely clear here. “We have a domestic inequality problem that people have now confused with a free trade problem.” The part after the first “problem” is wrong. We have confused unbalanced trade with free trade. FREE trade balances through currency. We have incentivized balance through sale of financial capital (stocks and bonds) and real estate, benefiting capital owners who import foreign labor in the form of goods and experience rising incomes through credit issued to an increasingly debt-burdened wage earners. I GET the libertarian argument. I was trained at the cathedral of it (Wharton). Everything moves in cycles. Intrusive and abusive government is a symptom of a fraying society. And to directly address the observation, yes we are a wealthy country (albeit less so on a relative basis than 50 and 100 years ago) and we benefit from trade. It’s not that other countries have “stolen” from us. It’s that we have allowed unbalanced trade to disproportionately benefit a global elite class that is now largely separate and distinct from their fellow countrymen (in both China and the U.S.) @michaelxpettis

entry.summary:
RT L0la L33tz If you, an unbiased person, take a look at this graphic by Elliptic, do you come to the conclusion that "unhosted wallets" are what enable cartels to launder money through cryptocurrencies? Or could it be that the actual problem is that cartels still somehow manage to deposit their cash in the financial system, despite extensive AML/CFT frameworks imposed on banks? And if these frameworks are already exploited by cartels, can you outline precisely how imposing these same AML/CFT regulations on "unhosted wallets" would stop cartels from exploiting them – and not just impose unproportionate burdens on the average user? Given what Elliptic has outlined in their newest report, lawmakers should be extremely wary of relying on for-profit marketing materials to inform their decisions, and keep in mind that the expansion of AML/CFT frameworks to "unhosted wallets" would drastically enlarge such firms' addressable market, constituting a clear profit motive – while likely doing nothing to stop actual crime.
The Rage: A new report by the Blockchain Surveillance firm Elliptic showcases how cartels exploit deficiencies in current AML/CFT frameworks, raising the question whether "unhosted wallets" are really the problem.
